attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both stated causes and the absolute 'any ability to learn or know anything'. Causal is the right kind.

contract.note: Reading 'any ability to learn' as measurable learning or retained information is an ordinary reading of a flat denial. The contract does not use performance to infer consciousness. The result depends on that reading.

evidence.note: GPT-3 paper (2020): primary experiments show abilities gained through training and better few-shot performance from examples. That refutes an absolute absence of learning.
T5 closed-book QA (2020): facts stored in model parameters answer questions, and the same models hallucinate. Knowledge and hallucination occur together.

reviews.rationale: The explanation depends on models having no ability to learn or know anything. Primary experiments that predate the post show learned, retained, usable information, and the same models still hallucinate. That meets the contract's contradiction condition. The consciousness part cannot be tested, but the categorical learning premise fails, so the causal account fails as stated.

semantics.note: 'Will now see his company publicly burn' is a firm forecast with a stated cause and a side effect on industry trust. The proposition keeps all three parts.

contract.note: The post came after the bad reviews, so 'will now' points to a future event. Reading 'publicly burn' as company failure is reasonable. The industry-trust part comes from the speaker's own words. No deadline was given.

evidence.note: Tom's Guide (Nov 2025) confirms unpaid staff and a strike. This shows serious distress, not collapse, cause or a trust effect.
Rabbit's own changelog: OS3 became generally available in Sept 2026. A company disclosure showing it is still operating.
TechSpot (Sept 2026): the company still operates and sells R1. Lyu's health claims are company statements.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. By the cutoff, Rabbit had financial distress and a staff strike but was still operating and shipping products. No terminal failure, causal link or industry-trust study is in the packet, and continuing to operate does not refute an undated forecast. The early-resolution rule is not met.

semantics.note: Under the policy, 'I would bet money' is a scored forecast. The proposition keeps 'try to charge', 'subscription' and the 'to stay afloat' purpose.

contract.note: Requiring an attempt at recurring fees, plus evidence of a survival purpose, follows the speaker's words. Whether a separate optional product counts is unclear, and the result depends on that.

evidence.note: June 2025: Rabbit launched paid Intern subscriptions with a promotion for R1 owners. It is a separate product, and there is no evidence it was meant to keep the company afloat.
Rabbit's own press release says R1 remains subscription-free and Intern is separate.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The Intern subscription is a possible candidate, but it is a separate optional product, R1 stays free, and nothing in the packet ties the fee to keeping Rabbit afloat. No wind-down occurred either. Neither early-resolution condition is met.

semantics.note: The proposition captures the capability claim and the decade-old comparison. It rightly leaves out the 'every single story' rhetoric.

contract.note: Splitting the claim into a capability part and a historical part is a fair reading. The contract specifies a mixed outcome if the parts diverge.

evidence.note: WebVoyager (Jan 2024) chooses and executes browser actions with measured task success. That goes beyond answering questions from a document, before the May 2024 post.
2011 technical account of Watson answering questions from text sources. Shows the capability existed more than a decade before the post. Written by an IBM researcher, so it is not fully independent.

reviews.rationale: The historical part holds: question answering over documents existed by 2011, more than a decade before the post. The core capability part is contradicted: agents available before May 2024 chose and executed web actions, not just document Q&A. As the contract specifies, opposing results give mixed.
